what_its_for: Clopidogrel is a blood thinner that helps prevent dangerous blood clots from forming in your blood vessels. It is used to lower your risk of having a heart attack or stroke, especially if you have had a recent heart attack, stroke, or a procedure called a stent placement. It works by keeping your blood platelets from sticking together and forming harmful clots.
how_to_take: Take clopidogrel exactly as your doctor tells you. Swallow the tablet whole with a full glass of water. You can take it with or without food. Try to take it at the same time every day to help you remember. Do not crush, chew, or split the tablet unless your doctor tells you it is okay.
dosing: The most common dose is one 75 mg tablet taken once daily. In some situations, such as after a heart attack or stent, your doctor may start you on a higher loading dose (such as 300 mg or 600 mg) and then switch you to 75 mg once daily. Always follow your doctor's specific instructions for your dose.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember on the same day. If it is already the next day, skip the missed dose and just take your next regular dose. Do not take two doses in one day to make up for a missed one. If you are unsure what to do, call your doctor or pharmacist.
storage: Store clopidogrel at room temperature, between 59°F and 86°F (15°C and 30°C). Keep it away from heat, moisture, and direct light. Do not store it in the bathroom. Keep all medications out of reach of children and pets. Dispose of any unused or expired medication safely through a drug take-back program.
what_to_avoid: Avoid taking aspirin, ibuprofen (Advil, Motrin), naproxen (Aleve), or other anti-inflammatory pain relievers unless your doctor specifically tells you to. These can increase your risk of bleeding. Avoid alcohol, as it can also raise your bleeding risk. Tell your doctor or dentist that you take clopidogrel before any surgery, dental procedure, or medical procedure, since it may need to be stopped temporarily. Do not stop taking clopidogrel without talking to your doctor first, as this could put you at serious risk of a heart attack or stroke.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away or go to the emergency room if you notice: unusual or heavy bleeding that will not stop, coughing or vomiting blood, blood in your urine (pink or red color) or dark tarry stools, severe headache, dizziness, or sudden weakness, signs of stroke such as sudden numbness on one side of your body, trouble speaking, or vision changes, or a serious skin rash or allergic reaction such as hives, swelling of the face or throat, or difficulty breathing. Contact your doctor if you have any dental work, surgery, or medical procedure scheduled.
when_it_works: Clopidogrel starts working to prevent clots within a few hours after your first dose. However, it may take several days to reach its full effect. It is important to keep taking it every day, even if you feel fine, because it is working quietly in the background to protect your heart and blood vessels.
special_populations: Older adults (65 and older): Clopidogrel can generally be used in older adults, but the risk of bleeding may be higher, so let your doctor know about any unusual bruising or bleeding. Pregnancy and breastfeeding: Tell your doctor if you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding. The safety of clopidogrel during pregnancy and nursing is not fully established, and your doctor will weigh the risks and benefits. Kidney or liver problems: If you have kidney or liver disease, tell your doctor, as this may affect how your body processes the medication. Genetics: Some people have a gene variation that makes clopidogrel less effective. If standard treatment does not seem to be working, your doctor may order a genetic test and consider an alternative blood thinner.
